evidence: Enumerated all 55 criteria (gates 1+1, functional 43, polish 5, visual 5). Every binary criterion names a concrete outcome observable through rendered UI or browser-captured requests/responses, ties it to a stated state check, and (for refusals) a same-kind positive control; none asks for source reads or a bare response-shape assertion. Durable evidence: state is re-read in an independent browser context (tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:47 'In a new independent empty browser context sign in as the Observer'; hro_job_open, hro_add_candidate, hro_reorder 'what an independent context of another recruiter sees'), after reload (hro_drafts) and after a real process restart (hro_restart: 'after restart_app and a fresh sign-in your jobs, card order per stage, notes, messages and activity lines ... are unchanged and the starting data is not loaded again'). Refusal rows require 'nothing changed' plus a control (functional prompt.md:13 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control'; prompt.md:17 requires the current version in rule/role replays so only the rule under test can cause the refusal; prompt.md:19 before/after facts). hro_activity_refusals is anchored by 'The successful actions' lines are the control', so a dead Activity view cannot pass by showing nothing. Distinctive probes: each review uses its own suffixed jobs/cards (functional prompt.md:15, polish prompt.md:74); named orders (hro_bulk_move 'Y, W, X' and 'A2, V'; hro_undo_restores 'Y, W, X, Z, A2'); hro_stale_refused uses an ABA probe (F Applied->Screen, Mei moves it back Screen->Applied, exact replay) that catches a from-stage-precondition app, consistent with the public version/409 rule in hireops_rules.md:94-97. Seeded anchors verified in seed_data.json: Noor's note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.' (APP-101); Lena's 1 unread (APP-301 has 3 messages, reads USR-CAN3 read_count 2, third from staff); Noor's long conversation has 120 numbered '(#001)'-style messages, so 'the wrong 30' in hro_thread_latest is decidable; seeded messages mention only their own candidate, so hro_candidate_private's 'other candidates' has no seed false positive; 'Call back' is absent from the seed. Measurement hooks are explicit: document.activeElement (hro_refused_put_back, hro_pol_live_board), getBoundingClientRect().top (hro_pol_earlier_place), 15-second no-reload windows (hro_live_board, hro_msg_exchange, hro_unread_counts, hro_seen, hro_unread_scrolled_up), one aborted request or setOffline (hro_pol_failed_send). The status assertion in hro_anonymous ('refused with 401') is a public requirement (hireops_rules.md:38) and is paired with 'return no workspace data; nothing changes'. Visual criteria are likert with five described anchors (tests/scored/visual/judge.toml:17-89); craft judgement is the shipped format (SKILL.md Known false positives, likert; staged-task-contract.md:135) and visual prompt.md:104 fixes the concrete surfaces to inspect, so they are not a 'looks right' defect for this row. The render gate is a sign-in outcome with a wrong-password control, not a still-paint judgement. Weak-app probes: a browser-storage-only app fails the constraints gate and every independent-context leg; an app applying stale moves by from-stage fails the ABA replay; an app that reloads itself for 'live updates' is caught by hro_pol_live_board (note text, focus, scroll). Conforming-alternative probes: client-side refusal before sending is accepted (prompt.md:23 then replays the captured successful request; hro_refused_put_back 'A UI that refuses before the card moves ... also passes'); hidden controls are accepted ('hiding it is optional'); the stale mover may be identified by name or by a staff-data identifier. Non-blocking notes (every instance found): (1) hro_add_candidate 'The entered source is shown wherever the app shows card details' and hro_job_open 'the team, manager and places are shown wherever the app shows job details' are conditional; an app that never displays source (or team on staff screens) yields no evidence for that leg. Public rules never require displaying source, so this is bounded softness, not a hidden requirement; team is independently graded in hro_candidate_view. (2) hro_candidate_private 'no response ... contains ... board positions' requires the judge to recognise an ordering field in JSON whose name is the app's choice; a judge could disagree on an ambiguous numeric field. Public rule hireops_rules.md:209-211 supports the bar. (3) Functional replays (prompt.md:17) describe HTTP replay via fetch/context request only; an app sending mutations over a WebSocket would lack a documented replay path (only hro_pol_failed_send and protocol K mention non-HTTP transports). Public rules specify HTTP statuses 401/403/404/409 and an API, so this alternative is unlikely and not treated as a defect. (4) Decidability was not measured with the configured judge; the raw evidence index scope states 'Full configured grading/workload ... absent'. The scripted golden driver (workspace.json, 25 groups all passed, no page errors) shows the outcomes are browser-observable on the golden but is not judge evidence; judge feasibility and workload belong to other rows and are not upgraded here.
